guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly UK market totals and trends do not establish availability, technology, or measured speed for an individual postcode or parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom updated the market data page on 23 July 2026.
UK fixed-voice service revenue was £891.9 million in Q1 2026.
Fixed-voice revenue decreased by £49.5 million, or 5.3%, from the previous quarter.
Fixed-voice revenue decreased by £194.2 million, or 17.9%, year on year.
The total number of fixed lines was 20.7 million at the end of Q1 2026.
Fixed lines fell by 757,000, or 3.5%, during the quarter.
Fixed-originated call volume was 3.32 billion minutes.
Fixed-originated call volume decreased by 583 million minutes, or 14.9%, year on year.
There were 29.4 million fixed-broadband lines at the end of Q1 2026.
Fixed-broadband lines increased by 282,000, or 1.0%, year on year.

guard_streams.write_limit: The public address checker combines available and planned status from supplier and OMR inputs; it is not accepted as exact corrected Ofcom r2 coverage or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: The GOV.UK gigabit address checker guidance was published on 13 March 2026.
The checker guidance was last updated on 7 July 2026.
The service is for addresses in England and Wales.
The checker reports whether gigabit broadband is available or planned for an address.
The displayed data is taken from the January Open Market Review.
The referenced January OMR was published in June 2026.
The guidance says the next checker update is due in September 2026.
The data is intended to be updated every four months thereafter.
The guidance warns that information may change when suppliers update delivery plans.
The guidance does not guarantee complete accuracy of an address's gigabit status.

guard_streams.source: Are you in or out of contract?
guard_streams.write_limit: Contract duration, notification, prices, and retail deals are consumer terms and do not establish physical broadband coverage or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom lists the contract-status guidance as last updated on 17 July 2026.
Phone, broadband and pay-TV contracts are typically 12, 18 or 24 months.
Leaving before the contract ends may trigger an early-termination charge.
Customers can check contract status through their provider's website, app or customer service.
Providers must tell customers when their contract is coming to an end.
Providers must remind customers who are already out of contract every year.
End-of-contract notifications must be sent between 10 and 40 days before the contract ends.
The notification must state when the contract ends.
The notification must state the current price and the price after the contract ends.
The notification must include best available deals and relevant bundled-contract end dates.

guard_streams.source: Telecoms price rises – what are your rights?
guard_streams.write_limit: Billing and contract-price rules are not broadband coverage, network availability, or parcel-measured speed evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom lists the price-rises guidance as last updated on 29 June 2026.
Since January 2025, new contracts cannot use inflation-linked or percentage-based price rises.
Specified in-contract price rises must be stated clearly in pounds and pence before sign-up.
Providers must state when any monthly-price change will take place.
Contracts signed before 17 January 2025 may still contain inflation-linked or percentage terms.
If the contract does not specify the rise, or the provider exceeds it, at least 30 days notice is required.
Customers must then be given 30 days to exit the contract.
A qualifying customer can leave without paying an exit fee.
The customer may choose a new contract with the same provider or switch provider.
Eligible customers should be able to move to their provider's social tariff without a penalty, even while in contract.

guard_streams.source: Use an Ofcom-accredited price comparison site to find the best deal
guard_streams.write_limit: Retail product comparison and accreditation do not verify that a specific network technology or speed is available at a parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom lists the price-comparison guidance as last updated on 17 July 2026.
Ofcom-accredited comparison sites undergo an audit.
The audit checks that information is accessible.
The audit checks that information is accurate.
The audit checks that information is transparent.
The audit checks that information is comprehensive.
The audit checks that information is up to date.
Broadbandchoices and MoneySuperMarket are listed for broadband, mobile, landline and pay-TV comparison.
Broadband Genie and broadbanddeals.co.uk are listed for broadband, landline and pay-TV comparison.
Ofcom separately directs users to its coverage checker to assess services available where they live.

guard_streams.source: Money saving tips for phone, broadband and pay-TV
guard_streams.write_limit: Money-saving, tariff, bundle and switching advice is retail context and cannot promote parcel coverage or accuracy.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the money-saving tips page on 1 July 2026.
People receiving certain benefits may qualify for a cheaper social tariff.
New-service contracts are typically 12, 18 or 24 months.
Providers must tell customers when contracts end and how much they could save on a new deal.
Ofcom advises out-of-contract customers to look for a better deal.
The guidance recommends using Ofcom's mobile and broadband checker for local service options.
The guidance recommends using comparison sites to review available retail offers.
Smaller providers may sometimes be cheaper and should be included in comparisons.
Ofcom says the new provider should manage the switching process.
Bundling services can be cheaper but may reduce flexibility.
